tasks.title: Define OS/system metric ingestion contract
tasks.problem: pgstat must distinguish PostgreSQL bottlenecks from host CPU, memory, disk, filesystem, and network bottlenecks without adding load to the target PostgreSQL database.
requirements: Define supported OS families and variants: Linux generic, RHEL/Rocky/Alma/CentOS/Fedora family, Ubuntu/Debian family, SUSE family, and Windows Server. Unsupported OS behavior must be explicit.
Define source adapters: optional read-only OS user collection, optional node_exporter/windows_exporter scrape/import, optional Telegraf/Prometheus bridge, and manual/API ingestion.
OS collection must not query or load the target PostgreSQL database. Only central pgstat storage may be written.
Direct OS collection must use least privilege. Default design should work with a read-only OS user and command/source allowlist; no root/sudo requirement by default.
Define host identity and OS change history so a machine can move from Windows to Linux, RHEL to Ubuntu, or similar without corrupting historical evidence.

Define PostgreSQL instance to host/container binding: automatic evidence-based matching, explicit manual override, binding confidence, ambiguity handling, valid_from/valid_to history, and no AI high-confidence use when binding is missing or low-confidence.

Define host service health observation for PostgreSQL-related services: PostgreSQL server, PgBouncer, Patroni, pgpool-II, HAProxy/Keepalived when tagged as PostgreSQL traffic components, and container/Kubernetes equivalents.

Define a fast service heartbeat separate from heavier OS metric cadence so stopped, failed, unhealthy, or restart-looping PostgreSQL-related services can alert quickly without querying the target PostgreSQL database.

Define minimum metrics: CPU/load/iowait/steal, memory/swap, disk IOPS/throughput/latency/utilization, filesystem bytes/inodes, network throughput/errors/drops, and optional PostgreSQL process CPU/memory where safely available.
Define missing/stale/partial coverage behavior. Missing OS metrics must never be silently treated as zero or healthy evidence.
Define schedule, retention, purge, partition, rollup, units, security, export, and AI evidence policy.

acceptance_criteria.text: Supported OS families, unsupported OS behavior, and OS change history model are documented.
Collection source adapters are documented with target DB load impact explicitly stated as zero.
Read-only OS user / least-privilege model is documented for direct collection.
Instance-host/container binding model is documented with automatic evidence sources, manual override, confidence levels, ambiguity behavior, and historical validity ranges.

PostgreSQL-related service health contract is documented, including service discovery sources, allowlist/tag model, status values, fast heartbeat cadence, alert transitions, and container/Kubernetes service health mapping.
Minimum metric list includes units, cadence, retention, purge, partition, and rollup decisions.
Missing/stale/partial metrics behavior is documented and blocks high-confidence findings when needed.
pgdbaagent optional evidence usage is documented without making OS metrics silently mandatory.

implementation_plan: Write the OS/system metric capability card and contract first.
Choose source adapter priority: API/import first, exporter bridge second, direct read-only OS user third unless customer accepts host access design.
Define dim.host_ref, host observation history, container observation history, instance_host_binding, metric naming, units, and retention before migration work.
Define binding precedence: manual binding, explicit agent claim, container/Kubernetes label, listener/process match, cloud tag, then unbound/ambiguous.
Define service observation as read-only state collection: systemd/Windows SCM/container runtime/Kubernetes status, no start/stop/restart actions, no shell execution by default.
Define fast service heartbeat targets and thresholds separately from OS metric collection to support quick alerts for PostgreSQL/PgBouncer service failure.
Document that OS collection must not add load to target PostgreSQL databases.
verification_plan: security review of direct OS collection model

tasks.title: Implement pgstat-node-agent V1
tasks.problem: pgstat needs an optional, low-overhead host agent to collect OS metrics, host identity, container context, and PostgreSQL-related service health without querying or loading the monitored PostgreSQL database.
requirements: Implement the official pgstat-node-agent path defined in docs/pgstat-node-agent-requirements.md.
Agent must not connect to the monitored PostgreSQL database, must not require DB credentials, and must not run diagnostic SQL.
Agent must collect host identity, OS observation, OS metrics, coverage state, and PostgreSQL-related service health.
Agent must support Linux host service deployment, Windows service deployment, and container/DaemonSet-style deployment according to the accepted contract.
Agent must push to central pgstat API using scoped ingest token and must mask secrets in logs.
Agent must support fast service heartbeat separately from heavier OS metric cadence.
Agent must not manage services. No start, stop, restart, or arbitrary shell execution in V1.
Docker socket access must be disabled by default and documented as optional high-privilege enrichment if ever enabled.
Missing, stale, partial, or unsupported metric coverage must be reported explicitly.

acceptance_criteria.text: Agent produces valid host identity, OS metric, service heartbeat, and coverage payloads accepted by central pgstat API.
Agent runs without target PostgreSQL credentials and no target PostgreSQL query/load is introduced.
Linux service, Windows service, and container deployment paths are documented and smoke-tested or explicitly phased.
PostgreSQL/PgBouncer/Patroni-style service health transitions are reported with fast heartbeat and central alert eligibility metadata.
Agent security model is verified: scoped token, secret masking, least privilege, no service management, no arbitrary command execution.
Coverage state distinguishes missing, stale, partial, unsupported, and healthy data sources.

implementation_plan: Create agent package after OS contract and central ingestion API are accepted.
Implement config, auth, TLS transport, bounded retry spool, and self-health first.

tasks.title: Raise a system alert when a ready instance loses pg_hba access, readable in Telegram and UI
tasks.problem: Customer-reported bug (2026-07-17), root-caused via systematic debugging: when a previously working instance loses its pg_hba.conf entry (or otherwise fails auth/connect), JobOrchestrator.processClusterInstance/processStatementsInstance catch the exception, call stateRepo.updateAfterFailure (consecutive_failures++), then call handleSecretOrAuthError which matches the message on 'connect'/'authentication'/'password'/'secret_ref' and calls inventoryRepo.scheduleBootstrapRetry — this flips instance_inventory.bootstrap_state to 'degraded'. findDueInstances only selects bootstrap_state='ready' (InventoryRepository.java:155), so the instance drops out of the collection queue on the very next cycle and consecutive_failures freezes (usually at 1). SystemHealthEvaluator.checkInstanceUnreachable only opens SYSTEM_INSTANCE_UNREACHABLE when consecutive_failures >= 3 (SystemHealthEvaluator.java:195), so the threshold is never reached. BootstrapHandler then silently retries the degraded instance on a backoff schedule (1min/5min/15min/1hour) with no alert at any point. Net effect: an instance could sit unmonitored indefinitely with zero Telegram/system alert, only an INFO log line ('Instance degraded'a cekildi'). Follow-up (2026-07-27): once the alert did fire, the customer reported it was uninterpretable in Telegram ('Instance unreachable ... The connection attempt failed.' with no host name anywhere) and the UI's InstanceDetail degraded-reason banner didn't recognize this alert code either.
requirements: Raise a system alert (reuse AlertCode.SYSTEM_INSTANCE_UNREACHABLE, critical) the moment an instance is pushed to degraded by handleSecretOrAuthError, including the classified error detail (pg_hba / auth / connect) in the alert message.
Auto-resolve that alert when the instance successfully returns to bootstrap_state='ready' (BootstrapHandler.handleEnriching).
Every instance-scoped system alert (not just this one) must show which host/instance is affected in the title, since Telegram/email only carry plain title+message text.
The UI's existing degraded-reason banner (InstanceDetail's BootstrapBanner) must also recognize this alert code, not just bootstrap-time codes.
Do not touch the existing bootstrap-time secret_ref_error alert path (BootstrapHandler catch blocks) — this fix targets only the post-ready degrade path in JobOrchestrator.
Keep the fix minimal: no new alert code, no new migration — reuse existing AlertService/AlertCode/notification plumbing and the existing BootstrapBanner UI component.

acceptance_criteria.text: handleSecretOrAuthError raises system_instance_unreachable with the classified error detail when it degrades an instance.
The alert auto-resolves once the instance reaches bootstrap_state='ready' again.

AlertService.upsertSystemAlert automatically appends the instance's display_name and host:port to the alert title when instancePk is provided, so this and every other instance-scoped system alert is readable in Telegram without opening the UI.
InstanceDetail's BootstrapBanner recognizes system_instance_unreachable and shows the same clear degraded-reason banner as the other bootstrap-failure codes.
mvn test and ui tsc pass; a live check confirms the Telegram message names the host and the InstanceDetail banner shows the reason for a real pg_hba revocation, and both clear on restore.

implementation_plan: Inject AlertService into JobOrchestrator's handleSecretOrAuthError (or a small helper) and call alertService.upsertSystemAlert with AlertCode.SYSTEM_INSTANCE_UNREACHABLE, alert_key 'system.instance_unreachable:instance=<pk>', including the raw exception detail.
Inject AlertService into BootstrapHandler and call alertService.resolveSystemAlert on the same alert_key inside handleEnriching right after the state flips to 'ready'.

Add AlertService.withInstanceLabel(title, instancePk): looks up control.instance_inventory (display_name, host, port) and appends '— <display_name> (<host>:<port>)' to the title; fails soft if lookup errors. Call it from upsertSystemAlert before insert/update.
Add 'system_instance_unreachable' to InstanceDetail.tsx's bootstrapCodes array so the existing BootstrapBanner picks it up.
Add/extend a unit test asserting the alert is raised on the degrade path and resolved on the ready transition (tracked as a known test-coverage gap alongside the rest of this code path).
verification_plan: Live: revoke pg_hba access for a test instance, confirm system_instance_unreachable opens with the host named in the Telegram message and the InstanceDetail banner shows the reason; restore access, confirm the alert auto-resolves and the banner clears.
verification_evidence: Root cause confirmed 2026-07-17 via systematic debugging (5 hypothesis-testing steps tracing JobOrchestrator -> InventoryRepository.findDueInstances -> SystemHealthEvaluator threshold -> BootstrapHandler retry loop).

Fix applied 2026-07-17: JobOrchestrator.handleSecretOrAuthError now raises AlertCode.SYSTEM_INSTANCE_UNREACHABLE (alert_key system.instance_unreachable:instance=<pk>) with the classified error detail; BootstrapHandler.handleEnriching resolves the same alert_key once the instance reaches bootstrap_state='ready'.

Customer-reported unreadable Telegram alert 2026-07-27 (no host name) led to a discussion and a centralized fix: AlertService.withInstanceLabel() added and wired into upsertSystemAlert; InstanceDetail.tsx bootstrapCodes now includes system_instance_unreachable.

mvn compile, mvn test, and ui tsc --noEmit all passed with no regressions (existing 4 collector test classes unaffected; this code path has no existing unit test coverage per docs/test-strategy.md known gaps).

Customer live-tested 2026-07-27 by revoking pg_hba for instance 'sam-ets': InstanceDetail showed the pg_hba error text in 'Son Hata' but bootstrap_state stayed 'discovering'/'ready' (never 'degraded') and no Telegram alert fired. Root cause #2 found: the instance had already gone ready->degraded->(auto retry)->pending->discovering, and DiscoveryCollector.discover()'s catch block (a completely separate code path from JobOrchestrator.handleSecretOrAuthError) only calls stateRepo.updateLastError (no alert, no consecutive_failures increment) when discovery fails — so an instance stuck retrying discovery forever raised zero alerts. Also, InstanceDetail's BootstrapBanner only rendered for bootstrap_state==='degraded', so even alerts raised on this path wouldn't have shown a banner for a 'discovering' instance.

Fix applied 2026-07-27: BootstrapHandler.handleDiscovering now calls a new raiseUnreachableAlert() helper (reusing AlertCode.SYSTEM_INSTANCE_UNREACHABLE, same alert_key pattern, so it still auto-resolves in handleEnriching) whenever discoveryCollector.discover() returns null, using the error text just written by StateRepository.getLastError() (new read-only method added). InstanceDetail's BootstrapBanner condition changed from bootstrap_state==='degraded' to bootstrap_state !== 'ready' (any not-yet-ready state), so the banner now also covers instances stuck retrying discovery.
mvn compile, mvn test, and ui tsc --noEmit all passed again after this second fix, no regressions.

Customer confirmed 2026-07-27 the alert now fires and names the host ('Instance unreachable — sam-ets (10.90.137.51:5432)'), but flagged the details view as noisy: the same long PostgreSQL error text was repeated 3-4 times (message body, 'Detay' panel's last_error, and a raw JSON block always shown below). Fixed: (a) collector alert messages (JobOrchestrator.handleSecretOrAuthError and BootstrapHandler.raiseUnreachableAlert) shortened to a plain-language sentence, with the technical error text left only in details_json.context.last_error; (b) Alerts.tsx AlertDetails: the raw JSON fallback is now hidden behind a collapsed '<details>/Ham veriyi göster' toggle whenever a readable panel (context/baseline/records) already shown that same data, instead of always rendering both; (c) the context.reason value ('discovery_failed' / 'degraded_after_ready') is now shown as a short Turkish label via a new reasonLabel() helper instead of the raw code.
mvn compile, mvn test, and ui tsc --noEmit all passed again after the message/UI cleanup, no regressions.

Customer reported 2026-07-27 (without having restored pg_hba access) that Telegram sent a 'Cozuldu' (resolved) notification for the same alert. Root cause #3: SystemHealthEvaluator.checkInstanceUnreachable() runs every 5 minutes and has a long-standing auto-resolve loop over ALL open SYSTEM_INSTANCE_UNREACHABLE alerts that closes any alert whose instance_state.consecutive_failures == 0 — regardless of why the alert was opened. The new BootstrapHandler.raiseUnreachableAlert() path (root cause #2's fix) never increments consecutive_failures (only JobOrchestrator.updateAfterFailure does), so any alert it opened had consecutive_failures==0 from the start and was auto-resolved by this unrelated 5-minute job within one cycle, while the instance was still genuinely unreachable.

Fix applied 2026-07-27: SystemHealthEvaluator.checkInstanceUnreachable()'s auto-resolve loop now also requires bootstrap_state == 'ready' (new isBootstrapReady() helper querying control.instance_inventory), not just consecutive_failures == 0, before closing a system_instance_unreachable alert. This makes the auto-resolve correct for both alert-opening paths: it no longer fires early for instances still stuck in 'degraded'/'discovering'.
mvn compile and mvn test passed again after this third fix, no regressions.
